publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Limited Motion Electrical Actuation Systems (DIgest No. 1998/494)
abstract: There is a growing need for programmable servo-controlled high-speed actuation in multiple axes, for applications as diverse as robotic manipulators, infrared and laser tracking systems, and automated manufacturing. At present, multi-degree-of-freedom motions are realised almost exclusively by using a separate motor/actuator for each axis, which results in relatively complicated and heavy transmission systems. This inevitably compromises the dynamic performance and servo-tracking accuracy, due to the combined effects of inertia backlash, nonlinear friction, and elastic deformation of gears. Actuators with multiple degrees-of-freedom should alleviate these problems, whilst being lighter and more efficient. However, although they have been the subject of research for several decades, and numerous concepts have been proposed, their application potential has not been realised, probably due to the complexity of their structure and related difficulties in modelling their electromagnetic behaviour and optimising their design. This paper describes two new forms of spherical actuator, and highlights the key design and operational issues.

articleTitle: Precision X-Y positioning systems using linear induction motors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Limited Motion Electrical Actuation Systems (DIgest No. 1998/494)
abstract: An X-Y stage for use principally in the semiconductor industry, for electron beam lithography tools and wafer steppers, is described. The stage features a moving puck which is supported by air bearings on a flat baseplate and is driven by on-board linear induction motors which thrust against the baseplate. The stage position is measured by laser interferometers and is controlled by a digital servo system which computes the drive to the linear motors in real time. The design and measured performance of the induction motors is described together with their 8 channel switch mode drive amplifier.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Limited Motion Electrical Actuation Systems (DIgest No. 1998/494)
abstract: Most linear, variable-reluctance, electromagnetic actuators utilise the 'tangential' or 'aligning' component of reluctance force. All of these devices are also exposed to a 'normal-force' of magnetic attraction which acts directly across the air-gap and does not contribute to the actuator output and is typically an order of magnitude greater than the mean tangential force. This unstable force has been exploited for decades, in an uncontrolled manner, over short stroke motions, e.g. in simple relays, but the authors decided to re-examine its potential in the light of modern electronics. The actuator harnesses this large force using a simple ratcheting design to integrate successive short strokes produced by the electromagnet. The novelty of this drive lies in the fact that it achieves blocking and ability to drive in either direction with only two operating coils.

articleTitle: Piezo actuators-can they give enough displacement for 'real world' applications?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Limited Motion Electrical Actuation Systems (DIgest No. 1998/494)
abstract: Piezoelectric stack or multi-layer actuators are capable of producing very large forces, but only minute displacements. Their very high rate of response and virtually zero steady-state power consumption make them potentially attractive for a wide range of machinery applications if their output displacements can be amplified to be useful in mechanisms constructed with normal engineering tolerances.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Limited Motion Electrical Actuation Systems (DIgest No. 1998/494)
abstract: An electro-rheological (ER) fluid per se is a semi conducting mixture of polarisable polymer particles of high dielectric constant and an insulating liquid of low dielectric constant. When an electric field is applied transverse to the direction of motion of the fluid, the resistance to flow is increased-in a passive fashion by inducing inter particle hydraulic action. The types of ER passive controllers explored so far are given. The squeeze film and Rayleigh types allow for but small displacements and are specifically associated with bearings.

articleTitle: Considerations of a short-stroke linear actuator
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Limited Motion Electrical Actuation Systems (DIgest No. 1998/494)
abstract: This paper outlines a study of a short-stroke rectilinear version of the Laws' relay actuator, for use in reciprocating electromechanical systems. Finite element analysis provides the static characteristics of the device, and the analysis is coupled to a nonlinear state-variable time domain simulation to determine the dynamic performance. Dimensional changes arising from a parametric study, together with the use of alternative magnetic materials, lead to a much improved performance. A comparison between simulated and measured results illustrates the accuracy of the modelling process.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Limited Motion Electrical Actuation Systems (DIgest No. 1998/494)
abstract: The subject of limited motion electromagnetic actuation systems is now very broad. It encompasses various enabling technologies and a wide range of magnetic circuit topologies, for an ever-increasing spectrum of applications spanning all market sectors. Thus, operational requirements vary widely, in terms of displacement, speed of response, positional accuracy, duty cycle and bandwidth. Further, whilst the majority of actuators have only a single degree-of-freedom, actuation systems are emerging which can provide multiple degrees-of-freedom of controlled motion. As a consequence, it is difficult to give a general overview of the current status of electromagnetic actuation systems. Therefore, the presentation focuses mainly on systems which have been the subject of research at the University of Sheffield, some of which have only been feasible because of the emergence of high energy permanent magnets. The following actuators are discussed: long-stroke and short-stroke actuators; solenoid actuators; active magnetic bearings; reciprocating actuators; and reciprocating generators.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Limited Motion Electrical Actuation Systems (DIgest No. 1998/494)
abstract: The availability of rare earth metals in commercial quantities lead to the discovery of highly magnetostrictive alloys containing terbium (Tb) and dysprosium (Dy) with iron (Fe). The first of the components generates the strains, the second minimises the field strengths required to generate the strains and the iron allows the alloy's exceptional transduction properties to be used at or above room temperature. The use of these materials for magnetostrictive actuators and applications of the actuators are briefly outlined.
